name: L-citrulline
summary: L-citrulline is an amino acid made by the body and involved in handling nitrogen. Supplements contain L-citrulline alone or citrulline malate, which also contains malate; their labelled amounts are not interchangeable.
commonUses: Used in pre-workout products marketed for exercise performance.
Used in products marketed for a muscle 'pump' during exercise.
roles: Citrulline participates in the urea cycle, which helps the body process waste nitrogen.
The body can convert citrulline to arginine, an amino acid used to make nitric oxide.

status.note: This basic guide does not provide a routine status test.

high.note: See the cautions below; this guide does not establish a safe upper amount.

forms.name: L-citrulline
forms.note: The single amino acid, without added malate.

forms.name: Citrulline malate
forms.note: Combines citrulline with malate. Total mixture weight is not the weight of L-citrulline; ratios and actual composition can differ between products.

reference.noUpperLimit: This basic guide does not provide reference intakes or upper-limit values.

cautions: Long-term safety information for citrulline malate is limited; short studies do not establish safety for ongoing use.
Some tested citrulline malate products did not match their stated ingredient ratios. A ratio on the label is not proof of the actual citrulline content.
Safety observations for L-citrulline alone cannot automatically be applied to a citrulline malate or multi-ingredient pre-workout product.

sources.title: A critical review of citrulline malate supplementation and exercise performance
